Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson characterized the draft as a 'framework agreement' and stated Iran's core position: ending the war on all fronts including Lebanon, lifting sanctions on Tehran explicitly included in the text, and a 30-to-60-day window for details to be negotiated before a final agreement. No statement has been issued by Supreme Leader Khamenei. No formal Iranian Foreign Ministry confirmation of the described text has been published. The structural constraint: nuclear issues are explicitly excluded from the current framework text. The congressional zero-enrichment constraint — 52 senators and 177 House members have publicly demanded zero enrichment as a condition — is not satisfied by a 30-60-day nuclear negotiation deferral. A framework that defers nuclear status to post-deal negotiations is categorically different from the Witkoff dismantlement demand that shaped the congressional letter. Even if the framework is announced and accepted, the WPA 90-day hard deadline on May 29 is not resolved by a deal declaration alone — Hormuz reopening and blockade lifting require physical implementation over days to weeks. The vibe signal: Trump public commitment + full coalition consultation + Iran FM 'framework agreement' language constitutes the strongest deal signal of the current cycle. The Fars dismissal and the absence of Supreme Leader or FM confirmation prevents a higher reading. Monitor for any Iranian Supreme Leader statement or formal FM response before Monday.
